title: Writing Don't Play Me Cheap with Harry Dial
summary: Randolph and Harry Dial wrote Don't Play Me Cheap, taking the title from a Chicago phrase about South Center department store.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, yes, Harry Dial Dow. Well, now, you mentioned him when you were in St. Louis.
And I noticed that 'Don't Play Me Cheap is written by you and Harry Dial Dew.
Yes, uh-huh, 'Don't Play Me -- that's right.
And I had a question here. Did that date from back in St. Louis, but now that you tell me that he was with the band on the road, did you write it on the road or did you write it a few years before?

In St. Louis. Wait a minute, 'Don't You Play Me Cheap, Don't Play Me Cheap,' wait a minute. No, I think we must have wrote that song, here, because I used to use that word, 'Don't Play Me (unintelligible), where (unintelligible), well, it's gone, anyway. It was a store, a department store by the name of -- you know the South Center, up there at 47th Street?
South Center. And the people use to say, used to make an expression, don't play me South Center,
meaning, don't play me cheap, you know.
And so, we just picked it up and wrote a song, 'Don't Play Me Cheap.'
